blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Pretraining generalist Earth observation foundation models requires data that combine several sensors, varied temporal sampling and, increasingly, text, yet open datasets rarely provide all three in one consistent, easily accessible form. We introduce MajorTOM:Elliot Pretrain, a collection of 279,166 tiles of 10 km drawn from the Major-TOM grid by clustering AlphaEarth embeddings. Each tile stacks Sentinel-2 L1C, Landsat-8/9, Sentinel-1 RTC, Copernicus DEM and ESA WorldCover on a shared 1056x1056-pixel, 10 m grid, complemented by cloud masks, OpenStreetMap entities and ERA5 weather. The tiles are partitioned into three temporal regimes, Monotemporal (250,000 tiles, one acquisition), Monthly (12,500 tiles, twelve acquisitions spread over the annual cycle) and Burst (16,666 tiles, six acquisitions within 30 days), and are released as 6.3 TB of Cloud Optimized GeoTIFFs indexed by TACO v3 Parquet metadata, a standard that allows cloud streaming, efficient data access, and filtering before any pixel is read. A companion library derives sensor-tagged fact sheets, captions and 16 families of vision-language tasks from these layers at load time. We test our design choices in short pretraining runs of OlmoEarth-Base. First, a 25% subset of Major-TOM Core-S2L2A curated with AlphaEarth embeddings matches or exceeds the full corpus on 8 of 9 benchmarks. Second, on Elliot-Pretrain, adding Landsat-8/9 improves or matches Sentinel-2 only pretraining on every benchmark. Third, using DEM and WorldCover as prediction targets during pretraining further improves 8 of 9 benchmarks, while giving the same maps to the encoder as inputs degrades 5 of 9. Fourth, Sentinel-1 helps on 7 of 9 benchmarks, particularly on benchmarks with radar inputs. Fifth, rule-based captions match a small language model at no cost. The dataset is openly available at https://source.coop/major-tom/elliot-pretrain.

blocks.en:
Earth observation satellites generate petabytes of unlabeled imagery every year,
making self-supervised geospatial foundation models (GFMs) the natural path to scalable EO intelligence.
However, AI-ready EO data has become a bottleneck for the development of GFMs for scientific
and operational applications Santoro et al. (2026) . Existing open pretraining datasets ( Francis and Czerkawski, 2024 ; Wang et al., 2023 ; Blumenstiel et al., 2025 ) provide scale and, in several
cases, more than one sensor, but they usually lack two things that GFM pretraining also needs. First, a
temporal structure that serves different training objectives at once: static global coverage, seasonal
cycles and rapid event dynamics, whereas most datasets apply one temporal sampling to every location.
Second, an access format that is modular and efficient, where sensors are stored independently and
combined on demand, and samples can be filtered before any pixel is read.

rather than one at the expense of the other, through the explicit
Monotemporal / Monthly / Burst regimes, with modality-tagged fact sheets from which vision-language tasks and captions are generated on the same tile grid. 2. Semantic diversity: Elliot-Pretrain uses embedding-based diversity (AlphaEarth ( Brown et al., 2025 ) + spherical k k -means) to select a diverse, semantically meaningful subset of the Major-TOM dataset Francis and Czerkawski (2024) . 3. blocks.en:
Building ML-ready pretraining corpora from EO archives is non-trivial: each sensor
arrives in its own projection, resolution, and file format, and combining them into
aligned, batchable tensors requires substantial engineering effort. A growing set of
open datasets has taken on that work and their design choices (which sensors to
include, how to store them, and how to select locations) directly shape what a
model trained on them can learn. Table 1 summarises how current datasets compare.

blocks.en:
In Francis and Czerkawski (2024) , the authors released Major-TOM, one of the largest open
ML-ready Sentinel-2 collections: 2.2M patches on a uniform 10 km grid, with
partial Sentinel-1 RTC and Copernicus DEM companions, totalling more than 60 TB.
Its bottleneck is I/O, not spatial coverage: each spectral band is stored as an independent
GeoTIFF blob in its own Parquet column with one row per row group. SatlasPretrain Bastani et al. (2023) is widely used and genuinely effective, spanning Sentinel-2, Sentinel-1, Landsat 8/9, and NAIP imagery with 302M labels across 137 categories. Those labels, however, are split across seven different per-task formats, so using it as an unlabeled multi-sensor corpus means reconciling seven representations before a single aligned batch can be built.

部分哨兵1号RTC和哥白尼DEM同伴,共计60多TB.
它的瓶颈是I/O,而不是空间覆盖:每个光谱带作为独立的存储.
GeoTIFF blob 在自己的 Parquet 列中,每行组有一行. SatlasPretrain Bastani等人(2023年)被广泛使用并真正有效,跨越了哨兵2号、哨兵1号、Landsat 8/9号和NAIP图像,标有302M的标签,共137个类别。 然而,这些标签分为7个不同的每个任务格式,因此,用它作为无标签的多传感器,意味着在建立单一对齐的批次之前调和7个表述。

blocks.en:
SSL4EO-S12 ( Wang et al., 2023 ) and TerraMesh ( Blumenstiel et al., 2025 ) target multimodal and multitemporal self-supervised pretraining. SSL4EO-S12 samples
251,079 locations worldwide and provides four seasonal acquisitions of co-located
Sentinel-1 GRD, Sentinel-2 L1C, and Sentinel-2 L2A imagery, distributed as plain
per-product GeoTIFF files with no unified index. TerraMesh is substantially larger, merging SSL4EO-S12 v1.1 with a filtered
subset of Major-TOM into approximately 9 million co-registered samples
across nine modalities (Sentinel-1 GRD/RTC, Sentinel-2 L1C/L2A, NDVI,
Copernicus DEM, ESRI LULC, and natural-language captions created by LLaVA-Next Li et al. (2024) and Overture Maps data Marimo et al. (2025) ). It applies one temporal strategy uniformly across all locations,
with S1/S2 pairs matched to within roughly one week of each other. It is the pretraining corpus behind TerraMind Jakubik and others (2025) . PhilEO ( Dionelis et al., 2025 ) pretrains on the full 23 TB Major-TOM Core-S2L2A, on FastTOM, a 2 TB land-only subset of it,
and on the 0.5 TB PhilEO Globe. The largest corpus helps only when model size grows with it,
and the seasonally structured PhilEO Globe, with four acquisitions per location, outperforms both
Major-TOM and FastTOM on land-cover mapping. This suggests that temporal structure can matter more
than raw scale, and that the benefit of scale depends on model size.

blocks.en:
On the language side, SkyScript ( Wang et al., 2024 ) turns 2.6M OpenStreetMap (OSM) OpenStreetMap contributors (2024) tags into rule-based captions, and OSMDA ( Ailuro et al., 2026 ) prompts a VLM to caption
OSM-rendered map tiles, alongside broader web-scraped RS caption datasets
(RS5M/GeoRSCLIP, GAIA). These are flat image-text collections distributed
independently of any multi-sensor pretraining corpus. TerraMesh takes a step toward
closing this gap by including captions ( Blumenstiel et al., 2025 ) , but its temporal
structure is uniform across all locations and its Zarr-based storage couples pixel retrieval to full archive loads, preventing the metadata-first filtering that TACO’s separated Parquet index enables. MajorTOM:Elliot Pretrain instead generates language from the dataset’s own metadata, across heterogeneous temporal regimes and with facts tagged by modality, so that captions and tasks follow any multi-sensor batch without coordinate reconciliation: a layout optimized for GFM adaptation to VLMs.

blocks.en:
MajorTOM:Elliot Pretrain is a multi-sensor, multi-temporal Earth observation
pretraining dataset built on the Major-TOM 10 km global grid ( Francis and Czerkawski, 2024 ) , distributed through Source Cooperative at source.coop/major-tom/elliot-pretrain under CC-BY-SA 4.0 (except its OpenStreetMap files and the facts/ folder, which are ODbL-1.0) (see Fig. 1 ). It is a single collection of three TACO v3 subdatasets (Monotemporal, Monthly and Burst). Each tile folder holds its sensor, cloud-mask, OpenStreetMap and administrative layers, and per-image metadata such as ERA5 weather. A top-level facts/ folder of precomputed fact sheets lets captions and tasks be generated without reading pixels. The three subdatasets
share a single tile identifier space and a common 1056 × 1056 1056\times 1056 -pixel, 10 m
spatial grid.

carries only scalar metadata (identifier, CRS, centroid, grouping codes) and no
pixels; it is defined by Sentinel-2’s orbital acquisition plan rather than an
external land mask.

blocks.en:
From this pool, 279,166 tiles are selected for semantic
diversity rather than geographic coverage: two tiles count as similar only
if a vision foundation model’s embeddings of their imagery are similar, independent
of ground distance. More specifically, every land-grid tile is embedded with AlphaEarth Foundations ( Brown et al., 2025 ) , chosen because it is a state-of-the-art GFM with publicly available embeddings (64-d, spatially averaged and renormalised to unit norm), and a two-level spherical k k -means hierarchy over the ≈ \approx 2.5M embeddings selects 279,840
representative tiles, one per fine cluster, in minutes rather than the hours a
flat k k -means at that scale would require (Appendix D ).
Intersecting these candidates against tiles present in both the Sentinel-2 and
Landsat-8/9 tables removes 674 high-latitude tiles lacking L8 coverage, leaving
279,166 tiles that are randomly split with a fixed seed into Monotemporal,
Monthly, and Burst at the proportions in Table 2 .
Monotemporal receives by far the largest share of the selected tiles because each additional acquisition of the same location is highly redundant with the previous ones, so temporal tiles add little new signal per byte and per training step, whereas Monthly and Burst are kept at a smaller size because many downstream tasks require temporal inputs and the model must learn what time means.

Temporal selection differs by regime. Monotemporal reuses each tile’s Major-TOM
image identifier if one already exists, for compatibility with prior
pretraining runs, and otherwise takes the least-cloudy available acquisition.
Sentinel-2 and Landsat-8/9 dates are chosen independently with no cross-sensor
alignment enforced. Monthly and Burst are both driven by Sentinel-2 acquisition
dates, chosen greedily to maximise temporal spread: circularly across the full
year for Monthly’s 12 slots and linearly within an automatically selected 30-day
window for Burst’s 6, with Landsat-8/9 matched to each date through a four-level
cascade of progressively relaxed temporal tolerance and cloud-free score threshold
(Appendix D ). A small number of tiles have no usable Landsat-8/9
acquisition: 26 of 12,500 Monthly tiles (all twelve images, 23 of them south of 60° S, where
WRS-2 is intrinsically gapped), 18 of 250,000 Monotemporal tiles and 3 of 16,666 Burst tiles (13 images). These are marked as nodata.

blocks.en: 2.3 Layers

Every tile holds the same set of layers on one shared 1056 × 1056 1056\times 1056 -pixel, 10 m grid: four sensor
images (Sentinel-2, Landsat-8/9, Sentinel-1, and the static DEM and WorldCover maps), and context
layers (cloud masks, ERA5 weather and OpenStreetMap) that are not sensor images but share the tile’s
grid and folder. Two rules apply to all sensor layers. First, each sensor fills the acquisition slots
of the tile’s regime (one in Monotemporal, 12 in Monthly, 6 in Burst) with a single image per slot,
typically the least cloudy one available. Second, if a sensor has no acquisition for a slot, the
image is still stored, filled with the nodata value, so that every tile has the same layout.

blocks.en:
Sentinel-2 L1C has bands at three native resolutions
(10, 20 and 60 m). The 20 and 60 m bands are brought to 10 m by integer pixel replication, without
interpolation, and all 13 bands are stored in one COG, scaled by 10,000 10{,}000 following the ESA convention.
Landsat-8/9 combines 9 optical (OLI) and 2 thermal (TIRS) bands in one 11-band COG; because the two
groups have different noise floors, they receive different bit-depth trims
(Appendix C ). 807 Monotemporal Landsat frames are OLI-only products whose
thermal bands 10 and 11 are zero. Landsat-8/9 gaps are more common than Sentinel-2 gaps, mainly at high
latitude, where the WRS-2 grid leaves areas that Sentinel-2’s wider swath covers.

OpenStreetMap is stored as vector data. Each tile has an osm.parquet of features (75.5 million entities in total) and an admin.parquet of administrative units

used in two steps. The extraction keeps all features above a small size limit, so that tasks such as
small-object detection can use ordinary features like a restaurant or a bus stop. When the task library
builds a tile’s fact sheet, a second, stricter selection keeps only the named features a description
should mention (Appendix E ).

The collection does not store captions. It stores the data needed to produce them,
and a code library ( majortom-elliot-tasks , MIT licence Image and Signal Processing Group, Universitat de València (2026) ) builds
text from the layers when it is needed, so the wording changes at every epoch. For each tile the library
assembles a fact sheet of everything measured: spectral indicators from Sentinel-2 and Landsat-8/9,
relief and land cover, named OpenStreetMap features, cloud fractions, ERA5 weather and Sentinel-1
backscatter, plus time-series facts for Monthly and Burst tiles. Every fact is tagged with the sensor
that supports it, so facts from a sensor the model is not given are dropped. From the sheet the library
generates 16 families of vision-language tasks (captioning, grounding, grids, numbers and time-series
questions), each scored from 0 to 1 by a rule for its answer shape; captions are written by a rule-based
template that uses no language model. Appendix F lists the task families and describes
the scoring and the template.

blocks.en:
MajorTOM:Elliot Pretrain is built around three design choices that apply uniformly
across all subdatasets and that together determine how training batches are
constructed.

MajorTOM: Elliot Pretrain 围绕三种统一应用的设计选择而构建
并共同确定培训批次是如何进行的
建造。

blocks.en:
Every sensor and context layer is stored in its own subfolder of the tile
( DATA/<tile>/s2/ , l8/ , s1/ , dem/ , lc/ , cloud_s2/ , cloud_l8/ ), with its own children__<layer>.parquet metadata table. A tile is
identified by its folder index within a regime, and majortom:code_10km gives its grid code. Because every
COG is already aligned to the same geotransform, layers combine into pixel-aligned tensors with no reprojection.
A user downloads only the regimes and layers they need, and a new layer can be
added as a further subfolder and metadata table alongside the existing ones.

blocks.en:
MajorTOM:Elliot Pretrain is organized into three regimes (Table 3 ). In each one a tile is a folder DATA/<tile>/ , named by an integer index, whose subfolders hold one file per acquisition: data.tif in Monotemporal and img_NN.tif (Monthly, Burst) for the rasters, with the elevation and land-cover layers stored once as main.tif . The collection occupies 6.27 TB (3.08 TB Monotemporal, 1.84 TB the Monthly and 1.35 TB the Burst) plus the facts/ folder.
A Sentinel-2 image takes 5.7 MB on average (against 29 MB uncompressed, 5 × 5\times ), Landsat-8/9 2.3 MB

The per-tile OSM and administrative tables average 77 and 14 KB. Averages are over 300 random Monotemporal tiles.
The metadata tables are plain Parquet files with 10,000 rows per row group; the join key is internal:parent_id : image rows point to their layer-folder row in children.parquet , whose internal:parent_id is the tile.

blocks.en:
We choose OlmoEarth, one of the best EO encoders in the literature, with open weights, recipes and code, available in several model sizes. We pretrain OlmoEarth Base from scratch with the official v1.2 recipe ( Allen Institute for AI, 2025 ; Allen Institute for AI, 2026 ) :
latent masked image modelling with a patch-discrimination loss and an InfoNCE term, AdamW (learning rate 10 − 4 10^{-4} , weight decay 0.02),
global batch 512, token budget 2250, a cosine schedule with warmup over 1.2% of the run, and fixed seed. The model has 88.8M parameters with Sentinel-2 as its only modality; the Experiment 2 models, which add modalities as encoder inputs or decoder targets, have 92.0M to 101.4M (Table 13 ). Only the data, the
modalities, the temporal partition and the number of steps change between runs. One epoch is 488 steps over the 250,000 monotemporal
tiles and 4,266 steps over Core-S2L2A, which represent 0.07% and 0.64% of the official 667,200 steps. We use short schedules to run many
experiments at low cost, and conclusions are limited to this regime. The ten-epoch runs of Appendix 3.2 (42,660 steps) reach 6.4% of the official training regime.

blocks.en:
After pretraining, the encoder is frozen. Each benchmark input is standardized with the benchmark’s own per-band
mean and standard deviation. On the pooled features we fit a k k -nearest-neighbour (KNN) classifier (EuroSAT, So2Sat, BrickKiln, BigEarthNet, TreeSatAI)
or a linear probe (segmentation and regression), and report the test score of the probe after its 50 training epochs (the validation score is computed once, at the end, so no epoch is selected; the KNN classifier has no epochs). The metrics are accuracy
(EuroSAT, So2Sat, BrickKiln), micro-F1 (BigEarthNet), macro-F1 (TreeSatAI), mIoU (PASTIS, MADOS) and RMSE (Open-Canopy in m,
BioMassters in Mg ha -1 , lower is better). We use nine benchmarks to evaluate Experiment 1 (Section 3.2 , Fig. 4 ) and Experiment 2 (Section 3.3 , Fig. 5 ). Models with a Sentinel-1 pathway are scored on the Sentinel-1+Sentinel-2 version of the benchmark if one exists. Each configuration is pretrained once. For the ten-epoch runs, each checkpoint is evaluated with three probe seeds (3622, 8956, 30991) and averaged. This measures probe noise only, because the encoder is fixed. Full details are in Appendix K and Appendix O .

blocks.en: 3 Results
blocks.zh: 3 结果

blocks.en: This section first describes the released collection through its statistics (Section 3.1 ): tile counts and geographic spread, acquisition dates, cloud cover, Sentinel-1 coverage and OpenStreetMap context. It then uses the collection for two pretraining experiments and a caption study. Experiment 1 asks how the size and curation of the pretraining data affect downstream accuracy (Appendix 3.2 ). Experiment 2 asks whether additional sensors (part a) and the Monthly and Burst temporal partitions (part b) help (Appendix 3.3 ). The caption study compares template captions with captions written by language models (Appendix 3.4 ). The pretraining experiments use short schedules and one run per configuration, and evaluate frozen encoders on nine downstream benchmarks (Section 2.5 ).

blocks.en: 3.2 Experiment 1: Pretraining data size and curation
blocks.zh: 3.2 实验 1: 预训数据大小和目录

blocks.en:
We ask whether more data, or better-curated data, helps to pretrain a GFM under the same pretraining regime. The curated subset is selected on the same principle as Elliot-Pretrain, hierarchical k k -means clustering of AlphaEarth embeddings (Sections 2.2 and K ), so this experiment is the evidence for that design choice, tested on a corpus whose full, unselected pool is available for comparison. We compare four sets drawn from Core-S2L2A: the full corpus, a random 25% subset, the AlphaEarth-curated 25% subset and 512 random tiles. Then we pretrain OlmoEarth for ten full-corpus epochs (42,660 steps) and evaluate every 4,266 steps. Training was done in two parts: five epochs (21,330 steps) with their own cosine schedule, then five more, resumed from the
step-21,330 checkpoint with the schedule recomputed over all 42,660 steps. Therefore, at step 21.3K the learning rate jumps back up to the midpoint of a cosine and decays again. Figure 4 shows the scores at every checkpoint. To support the comparisons we run a paired t t -test over the ten checkpoints, comparing two runs at the same checkpoint, and report the mean difference with its 95% confidence interval (CI) in Table 16 ; the number above each panel is this mean difference to the 100% run, with ∗ for p < 0.05 p<0.05 and ∗∗ for p < 0.01 p<0.01 .
The curated 25% subset is significantly better than the full corpus on MADOS ( + 2.32 +2.32 points, CI [ + 1.78 , + 2.87 ] [+1.78,+2.87] ), BigEarthNet ( + 0.99 +0.99 , [ + 0.71 , + 1.28 ] [+0.71,+1.28] ) and So2Sat ( + 0.59 +0.59 , [ + 0.02 , + 1.17 ] [+0.02,+1.17] ). It is indistinguishable from it (CI includes zero) on EuroSAT, BrickKiln, TreeSatAI, Open-Canopy and BioMassters, and worse only on PASTIS ( − 3.15 -3.15 , [ − 4.46 , − 1.83 ] [-4.46,-1.83] ). It is therefore competitive with or better than 100% on 8 of 9 benchmarks. At the last checkpoint the extreme gaps are + 1.93 +1.93 in MADOS and − 1.01 -1.01 in PASTIS.
Compared directly with the random 25% subset (last column of Table 16 ), the curated subset is better on MADOS ( + 3.09 +3.09 , [ + 2.35 , + 3.83 ] [+2.35,+3.83] ), BigEarthNet ( + 0.68 +0.68 ), BrickKiln ( + 0.62 +0.62 ) and TreeSatAI ( + 0.13 +0.13 ), level on So2Sat, EuroSAT and the two regression tasks, and worse on PASTIS ( − 1.98 -1.98 , [ − 3.46 , − 0.49 ] [-3.46,-0.49] ). The advantage over random selection is real on four benchmarks but not uniform.
The 512-tile run is significantly worse than 100% on MADOS ( − 3.93 -3.93 ), EuroSAT ( − 1.38 -1.38 ), So2Sat ( − 1.30 -1.30 ) and TreeSatAI ( − 0.33 -0.33 ), with a final-checkpoint gap of up to 6.57 6.57 points in MADOS, but level on BigEarthNet ( − 0.02 -0.02 ), PASTIS ( + 0.04 +0.04 ) and BrickKiln ( + 0.89 +0.89 , [ − 0.04 , + 1.83 ] [-0.04,+1.83] ). Those tasks may be less sensitive to scale.
These intervals are over checkpoints of runs that were each pretrained once and no correction is made for multiple comparisons, so they describe the training trajectory and not the variation between pretraining seeds (Appendix N ).
blocks.zh:
我们问,更多的数据或更精确的数据是否有助于在相同的预训制度下预先培训一个全球调频系统。 所编译的子集与Elliot-Pretrain,分级k-指将AlphaEarth嵌入物集群(第2.2和K节)一样的原则被选中,因此这一实验是设计选择的证据,在一个有完整的,未选取的集合可供比较的体上测试. 我们比较了从 Core-S2L2A 抽取的四组:全体,随机25%的子集,AlphaEarth 校准的25%子集和512个随机瓦片. 然后我们预演了奥尔莫地(OlmoEarth)的十个全军纪(42,660步)并每4,266步评价一次. 培训分两部分进行:五个世纪(21 330步),有各自的余弦计划,然后再有五个,从2004年开始恢复。
检查点为21 330步,时间表为42 660步。 因此,在21.3K步骤上,学习率会回升到一个余弦的中点并再次衰败. 图4显示每个检查站的分数。 为了支持我们的比较,我们在10个检查站进行了对一对t-t的测试,在同一检查站进行了两次测试,并在表16中报告其95%的置信间隔(CI)的平均差值;每个面板上的数字是100%运行的这个平均差值,其中 * 在p < 0.05 p < 0.05, 在p < 0.01 p < 0.01 > 0.01。
配制的25%子集比MADOS(+ 2.32+2.32分,CI [+ 1.78,+ 2.87] [+1.78,+2.87]),大地网(+ 0.99+0.99, [+ 0.71,+ 1.28])和So2Sat(+ 0.59+0.59, [+ 0.02,+ 1.17] [+0.02,+ 1.17]))上的完整子集要好得多。 在最后一个检查站,MADOS的极端缺口是+1.93+1.93,PASTIS的为−1.01-1.01。
与随机的25%子集(表16上一栏)相比,所编的子集在MADOS(+ 3.09 + 3.09, [+ 2.35, + 3.83] [+2.35,+3.83]), BigEarthNet(+ 6.68 + 0.68), BrickKirn(+ 0.62 + 0.62)和 TreeSatAI(+ 0.13 + 0.13), So2Sat, EuroSAT和两个回归任务上较好,更糟糕的是PATIS(− 1.98-1.98, [− 3.46,− 0.49] [-3.46,-0.49]). 相对于随机选择而言,四个基准的优势是真实的,但不是统一的。
在MADOS(− 3.93-3.93)、EuroSAT(− 1.38-1.38)、So2Sat(− 1.30-1.30)和TreeSatAI(−0.33-0.33)上,512-瓦跑比100%严重得多,在MADOS中,最后检查点差距可达6.57 6.57分,但在BigEarthNet(−0.02-0.02)、PATIS(+0.04+0.04)和BrickKirn(+0.89+0.89)、[−0.04,+1.83][0.04+1.83]上,这些任务可能不太敏感。
这些间隔是在每次预先训练一次的跑道检查站上空,没有为多重比较进行更正,因此它们描述了训练轨迹,而不是预先训练种子之间的变化(附录N)。

blocks.en: Regression tasks (Open-Canopy, BioMassters) show near-zero differences across all conditions (every CI includes zero), and training steps seem to matter much more than which tiles were used. We observe that with more data, the frozen features separate BrickKiln slightly worse as training goes on. With 512 tiles they get slightly better. The fall is mostly in the first 17k steps. The curated subset favors rare landscape types and drops many near duplicate typical scenes. PASTIS is crop parcels in France, so it may rely on exactly those typical agricultural scenes, which could explain a slower start on PASTIS, and the high performance of MADOS. Nevertheless, this experiment would benefit from a more expensive longer pretraining comparison as it is still about 6.4% of the official OlmoEarth step count.
blocks.zh: 后退任务(Open-Canopy, BioMassters)在所有条件下(每个CI包括0)显示近乎零的差异,培训步骤似乎比使用哪块瓷砖更重要. 我们发现,有了更多的数据, 冰冻的特征 分开了BrickKirn 稍差一点 随着训练的进行。 有了512块瓷砖,它们会稍微好一些。 秋季大都为前17k步. 被整理的子集偏好稀有地貌类型并减少出许多相近的重复的典型场景. PASTIS是法国的收割地块,因此它可能依赖于这些典型的农业场景,这可以解释PASTIS的起步较慢的原因,以及MADOS的高性能. 然而,这一实验将受益于更昂贵的训练前比较,因为它仍然占奥尔莫地表正式步骤数的6.4%。

blocks.en: 3.3 Experiment 2: Sensors and temporal partitions
blocks.zh: 3.3 实验 2:传感器和时间分隔

blocks.en: We ask how useful additional sensors and time series are across diverse benchmarks. The experiment has two parts, (a) and (b), both shown in Figure 5 . Every model is OlmoEarth Base pretrained on its own pool of tiles and scored at step 488: one epoch for the Monotemporal pool, about 8.7 epochs for monthly+burst, and 95% and 90% of one epoch for mono+monthly and mono+monthly+burst.
blocks.zh: 我们问额外传感器和时间序列如何跨越不同的基准。 该试验有两个部分,即(a)和(b),均如图5所示。 每个模型都是OlmoEarth Base在自己的瓷砖池上预先训练,并在第488步打出分数:Monotemporal游泳池一个时段,月分+burst大约8.7个时段,单月分和单月分+burst一个时段95%和90%.

blocks.en: All models in (a) are trained on the 250,000 monotemporal Elliot-Pretrain tiles (one acquisition per tile, T = 1 T=1 ) for 488 steps. Starting from Sentinel-2 alone, we add Landsat-8/9, Copernicus DEM, ESA WorldCover and Sentinel-1 cumulatively. Sentinel-2, Landsat-8/9 and Sentinel-1 are encoder inputs (enc). DEM and WorldCover are decoder-only (dec), as in OlmoEarth: the encoder never sees them and the decoder only predicts them from the visible Sentinel-2 and Landsat-8/9 patches, so they act as auxiliary targets that are not needed at test time. We also test the opposite choice, giving DEM and WorldCover to the encoder as extra input (enc).
blocks.zh: (a)中的所有型号都经过了25万个单相的艾略特-普雷特列车瓷砖(每瓷砖一次获得,T=一T=一)的培训,共488个步. 从Sentinel-2开始,我们添加了Landsat-8/9,哥白尼DEM,ESA WorldCover和Sentinel-1,累计. Sentinel-2,Landsat-8/9和Sentinel-1是编码器输入(enc). DEM和WorldCover是只解码器的(dec),如在OlmoEarth中:编码器从未见过它们,而解码器只从可见的Sentinel-2和Landsat-8/9补丁来预测它们,因此它们作为测试时不需要的辅助目标. 我们还测试相反的选择,将DEM和WorldCover作为额外的输入(enc)给予编码器.

blocks.en: The reference in (b) is the S2+L8+DEM(dec)+WC(dec) model of (a), trained on monotemporal tiles only. We keep the model and the sensors and change only the tile pool: monthly+burst uses only the 12,500 monthly and 16,666 burst tiles, with no monotemporal tile (29,166 tiles, repeated until 488 steps); mono+monthly adds the monthly tiles to the monotemporal ones (262,500 tiles, 512 steps per epoch); mono+monthly+burst uses all three (279,166 tiles, 545 steps per epoch). All models in (b) are scored at step 488, so they receive the same number of updates as the reference. Temporal samples are padded to 12 timesteps and share the token budget, so a sample trades spatial extent for sequence length; in the two mixed pools a monotemporal tile has one real timestep and eleven padded ones.
blocks.zh: (b)中提及的是(a)的S2+L8+DEM(dec)+WC(dec)模型,该模型只受过一时用瓦片的培训。 我们保留了模型和传感器,只更换了瓷砖池:月+起爆只使用12,500个月和16,666个爆破的瓷砖,没有单相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相 (b)中的所有型号都是在第488步得分,因此它们得到的更新数量与参考数量相同. 时间标本被加到12个时间步并共享符号预算,因此一个样本会用空间范围来交换序列长度;在两个混合池中,一个一时平面有1个实时时间步和11个相加.

blocks.en: Figure 5 and Appendix O give the results. Adding Landsat-8/9 alone already brings much of the gain: it improves 7 of the 9 benchmarks, ties on 2 and loses on none relative to Sentinel-2 only. Adding DEM and WorldCover as decoder-only targets on top of Landsat-8/9 improves 8 of 9 benchmarks, most on PASTIS ( + 15 % +15\% ), and loses only on So2Sat ( − 2 % -2\% ). Giving them to the encoder instead is worse on 5 of 9, most on So2Sat ( − 14 % -14\% ). This supports treating DEM and WorldCover as decoder only targets for this benchmark suite, and shows that how a modality is added matters. The ladder is not monotone: the S2+L8+DEM model is worse than both of its neighbours on So2Sat, PASTIS, MADOS and Open-Canopy.
blocks.zh: 图5和附录 O给出结果。 仅添加Landsat-8/9就已经带来很多好处:它改善了9个基准中的7个,在2个基准上的联系,并且仅相对于哨兵-2没有损失。 在Landsat-8/9上添加DEM和WorldCover作为唯一的解码器目标,改进了9个基准中的8个,大多数是PASTIS(+15%+15+),并且只在So2Sat上输了(-2%-2+). 在九分之五的编码器上, 这支持将DEM和WorldCover只作为这个基准套件的解码器,并显示一种模式是如何被添加的. 梯子不是单通:S2+L8+DEM模式比其在So2Sat,PASTIS,MADOS和Open-Canopy上的相邻者都差.

blocks.en: Sentinel-1, together with L8, DEM and WorldCover, helps on 7 of 9 benchmarks, most on TreeSatAI ( + 11 % +11\% ) and BioMassters ( + 7 % +7\% ), ties on 1 and loses on So2Sat ( − 5 % -5\% ). It gives more consistent results than S2+L8+DEM(enc)+WC(enc), although So2Sat shows that it can also hurt, possibly on benchmarks scored with optical input only.
blocks.zh: 哨兵1号与L8、DEM和WorldCover一起,帮助了9个基准中的7个基准,大多数基准是:TreeSatAI(+11%+11++)和BioMassters(+7%+7++),关系在1上,在So2Sat上输了(-5%-5++). 它给出的结果比S2+L8+DEM(enc)+WC(enc)更一致,虽然So2Sat显示它也可能伤害到,可能只用光学输入得分的基准.

blocks.en: The multiclass segmentation benchmarks PASTIS (19 classes) and MADOS (15 classes) are the most sensitive. They gain from Landsat-8/9 ( + 9 % +9\% and + 5 % +5\% ) and from decoder-only DEM and WorldCover ( + 15 % +15\% and + 7 % +7\% ), lose when those layers go to the encoder ( − 12 % -12\% and − 11 % -11\% ), and are the most affected by the temporal partitions. The scene-level classification benchmarks (EuroSAT, BrickKiln, BigEarthNet, TreeSatAI) and the two regression benchmarks (Open-Canopy, BioMassters) change by 2 to 4% on average.
blocks.zh: 多阶级分化基准PASTIS(19个班)和MADOS(15个班)是最敏感的. 它们从Landsat-8/9(+9%+9++++5%++5+++)以及解码器唯一的DEM和WorldCover(+15%+15+++++7%+7++++)中得益,当这些层去到编码器(-12%-12%-++++++和-11%-11+++)时会失去,并且是受时分影响最大的. 场景级分级基准(EuroSAT, BrickKilln, BigEarthNet, TreeSatAI)和两个回归基准(Open-Canopy, BioMassters)平均变化2%至4%.

blocks.en: Relative to the monotemporal reference, every temporal partition lowers the score on most benchmarks (panel b). The largest losses are on PASTIS ( − 23 % -23\% for monthly+burst, − 45 % -45\% for mono+monthly, − 41 % -41\% for mono+monthly+burst) and MADOS ( − 2 % -2\% , − 23 % -23\% , − 18 % -18\% ). BigEarthNet ( − 2 % -2\% to − 10 % -10\% ) and BioMassters ( − 1 % -1\% to − 6 % -6\% ) fall less, and the other benchmarks stay within about 6% of the reference. The only gain is + 2 % +2\% on EuroSAT with monthly+burst. Monthly+burst, the only pool without monotemporal tiles, loses least on most benchmarks. This does not show that time series carry less information: samples are padded to 12 timesteps, they share the token budget, and OlmoEarth encodes the absolute acquisition date of each step. The temporal part needs more tests, for example pretraining with the years of the monthly timestamps rebased to one common year (the 12 acquisitions of a tile come from different years).

blocks.en: 3.4 Captions: template versus LLM
blocks.zh: 3.4 说明:模板与LLM

blocks.en:
We compare the template with the three LLM captioners of Section 2.5 , all writing from the same fact sheet. We took 100 stratified tiles and compared the four methods blind. Claude Opus 5.5 judged each
caption, with the image and the fact sheet as reference, on five axes, each scored from 0 to 10 (accuracy, coverage, salience,
spatial description and fluency), and counted the factual errors. We report the five scores, their mean and the errors per
tile in Table 5 . The table also lists the API cost of the captions, as a reference for users who want to generate them with an LLM. The cost is the estimated price of writing captions for all 279,166 tiles.
blocks.zh:
我们比较模板与第2.5节的三个LLM标题,都来自同一概况介绍。 我们拿了100块分层的瓷砖 将四种方法比作盲从 Claude Opus 5.5 判断每个
标题,以图像和概况介绍作为参考,在五个轴上,每个轴从0到10分(准确、覆盖、突出,
并计算出事实错误。 我们报告5分,他们的中分和错误
表5中的瓷砖。 该表还列出了标题的API成本,作为想要用LLM生成标题的用户的参考. 费用是所有279 166块瓷砖的书写标题的估计价格。

sheet and the four captions in random order. It scored each caption on five axes (0–10),
listed its factual errors, and ranked the four. Values are means over tiles, with
bootstrap 95% confidence intervals in brackets. Costs are the measured API cost of these 100 captions (OpenRouter), scaled linearly. Best value per row in bold.

blocks.en: Table 5 shows the results. The template, which is free, ties with the small LLM (mean score 7.26 for both), with a similar number of errors per tile (0.65 against 0.72), so the small LLM adds nothing over it. The large LLM is better by about one point (8.25) and with fewer errors (0.40 per tile). Adding the image to the large LLM does not change the scores on average (8.24 against 8.25). Since the difference between them is not great, we use the template in the library, so that captions are free and reproducible. Because the fact sheet is plain text, anyone can also generate captions from it with the LLM of their choice and pass them to the library; the table shows what to expect from a small and a large model. Three template examples with their judge scores are in Section G .
blocks.zh: 表5显示结果。 模板是免费的,与小LLM(两者的平均值为7.26分)有联系,每平板的出错数相近(0.65对0.72分),所以小LLM在上方没有增加任何. 大型LLM比相差约一分(8.25分),出错较少(每瓦0.40分). 将图像添加到大型LLM不会平均改变分数(8.24比8.25). 由于两者的区别并不大,所以我们在库中使用模板,这样字幕就可以免费再出. 由于概况介绍是纯正的文本,任何人都可以使用自己选择的LLM从中生成标题并传递到文库;表格显示从一个大小模型中可以期待什么. G节有3个附有其评委分数的模板示例。

blocks.en: There are some limitations. The comparison uses 100 tiles and one judge, which is itself a language model. It is not a downstream test: we did not train a vision language model on these captions, so we do not claim that a one point difference changes what a model learns.
blocks.zh: 有一些限制。 比较使用100块瓦和1个裁判,这本身就是一种语言模型. 这不是一个下游测试:我们没有在这些标题上训练一个视觉语言模型,所以我们不声称一个点的差异会改变一个模型学到的东西。

blocks.en: 4 Discussion
blocks.zh: 讨论

blocks.en: 4.1 Intended Use, Limitations and Biases
blocks.zh: 4.1 预期使用、限制和比喻

blocks.en:
The collection is meant for self-supervised pretraining of multi-sensor and
multi-temporal models, for controlled ablations over sensors and temporal regimes, and, through the task and captions,
for weak supervision and language grounding. WorldCover and the OSM entities are map products with their own errors, so they are suitable as pretraining targets and weak labels but not as reference labels for benchmarking.
blocks.zh:
该集旨在对多传感器进行自我监督的预训和
多时段模型,用于控制传感器和时间系统的分解,并通过任务和标题,
弱监管和语言基础。 WorldCover和OSM实体是带有自己出错的映射产品,因此适合作为预训目标和弱标签,而不能作为基准的参考标签.

blocks.en:
The tiles follow Sentinel-2’s acquisition footprint between
80° S and 84° N, so they include coasts and some open water, and 15.6% of the
Monotemporal tiles lie poleward of 60°, where Sentinel-1 VV+VH is mostly absent. The selection
is by diversity in AlphaEarth space, not by area. The selection therefore rebalances the collection
towards rare landscape types rather than reducing the typical distance.
blocks.zh:
瓦片跟随哨兵2号的收购足迹
南纬80°和北纬84°,因此包括了海岸和一些开阔水域,以及15.6%

blocks.en: Monotemporal images are selected to be clear (by CloudScore+), so the regime under-represents cloudy conditions, which only Monthly and Burst retain. The Sentinel-2 and Landsat-8/9 dates of a Monotemporal tile are chosen independently, and the Sentinel-1 pass can lie far from the Sentinel-2 date (90th percentile 162 days in that regime). Sentinel-2 is top-of-atmosphere L1C, with atmospheric correction left to the user. Its 20 and 60 m bands are replicated to 10 m and the 30 m Landsat and elevation layers are interpolated, so their effective resolution is coarser than the grid. The Landsat stack mixes top-of-atmosphere reflectance (bands 1 to 9, from the optical OLI) and brightness temperature in kelvin (bands 10 and 11, from the thermal TIRS). All eleven bands are stored as 32-bit integers with the same ×10,000 scale, so the thermal values are about 2.9×10 6 and differ by orders of magnitude from the reflectance bands; a single normalisation across the bands is wrong and per-band statistics should be used. A few tiles have no usable Landsat-8/9 acquisition (26 of 12,500 Monthly tiles, mostly in Antarctica, 18 of 250,000 Monotemporal tiles and 3 of 16,666 Burst tiles); fully missing images are stored as all-zero rasters with null product fields and l8:nodata_pct equal to 1, and the others have at least 90% nodata pixels.

blocks.en: 4.2 Summary of findings
blocks.zh: 4.2 调查结果摘要

blocks.en:
Three findings stand out. First, in our short, single-run setting the amount of unique pretraining data was not the limiting factor. A curated 25% subset of Core-S2L2A (AlphaEarth embeddings) is better than the full corpus on three benchmarks (MADOS, BigEarthNet, So2Sat), statistically level on five and worse on PASTIS ( − 3.15 -3.15 points); it is better than a random 25% subset on four benchmarks and worse on PASTIS; and 512 random tiles are worse than the full corpus on four benchmarks. At the last checkpoint the largest gap to the full corpus is 6.57 points (MADOS, 512 tiles).
Second, how a modality is added matters. Landsat-8/9 improves 7 of 9 benchmarks and loses on none. DEM and WorldCover as decoder-only targets improve 8 of 9 (up to + 15 % +15\% on PASTIS), whereas giving them to the encoder is worse on 5 of 9 ( − 14 % -14\% on So2Sat, − 12 % -12\% on PASTIS, − 11 % -11\% on MADOS). Sentinel-1 helps on 7 of 9 benchmarks, particularly on benchmarks with radar inputs such as TreeSatAI and BioMassters. The Monthly and Burst partitions lower most scores, a result confounded by padding and the token budget, so the temporal part needs more tests.
Third, a rule-based template already produces captions that tie with a small LLM (mean score 7.26 for both), a large LLM adds about one point (8.25) and lowers the errors per tile from 0.65 to 0.40, and adding the image to the prompt does not change the scores; since captions are generated from plain-text fact sheets, anyone can use the LLM of their choice.
The experiments are short (0.07% to 6.4% of the official schedule) and use one pretraining run per configuration, so we read them as indicative and not as a ranking of data or design choices.

blocks.en: 4.3 Limitations of the experiments
blocks.zh: 4.3 试验的局限性

blocks.en: The runs from the experiments use 0.07% to 6.4% of the official OlmoEarth schedule, each configuration is pretrained once, and encoders are frozen with one model family (OlmoEarth Base), so the results describe this early-training regime and not converged models. The confidence intervals in Experiment 1 are over the ten checkpoints of one run, include no pretraining-seed variation and are not corrected for multiple comparisons, and the three probe seeds change the nearest-neighbour scores by at most 0.1 points (So2Sat) and the linear-probe scores by at most 0.43 points (MADOS). The experiments also have confounds: Core-S2L2A (L2A) and Elliot-Pretrain (L1C) differ in processing level and are used in different experiments, the curated subset depends on one embedding model (AlphaEarth), and the temporal partitions are confounded by padding, the shared token budget and the span of years of the monthly tiles; all temporal models are scored at step 488, so the monthly+burst model sees its 29,166 tiles about 8.7 times, whereas mono+monthly and mono+monthly+burst stop before the end of their single epoch (at 488 of 512 and of 545 steps, 95% and 90% of it). Finally, the captions are judged on 100 tiles by one language model, and no vision-language model was trained on them. We therefore read the results as indicative, not as a ranking of data, sensors or captioners.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusions
blocks.zh: 5. 结论

blocks.en: We presented MajorTOM:Elliot Pretrain, a collection of 279,166 tiles selected by clustering AlphaEarth embeddings of the Major-TOM land grid. Each tile holds Sentinel-2 L1C, Landsat-8/9, Sentinel-1 RTC, Copernicus DEM and ESA WorldCover on one 1056 × 1056 1056\times 1056 -pixel, 10 m grid, together with cloud masks, ERA5 weather and OpenStreetMap context, in three disjoint temporal regimes (Monotemporal, Monthly and Burst) released as three TACO subdatasets of Cloud Optimized GeoTIFFs, whose Parquet metadata can be filtered before any pixel is read and whose layers can be downloaded and combined independently. Checks on the metadata of every tile and on the pixels of 300 random tiles show that all layers share one grid, that the metadata match the pixels, and that the cloud masks agree with the independent CloudScore+ score (Spearman 0.84 for Monthly and 0.73 for Burst). Moreover, text is not stored: the majortom-elliot-tasks library generates sensor fact sheets, tasks and captions from the data.

blocks.en: The experiments with OlmoEarth Base suggest three points. First, selection by embedding diversity can shrink a pretraining corpus with little loss: in ten-epoch runs, an AlphaEarth-curated 25% subset of Core-S2L2A was not worse than the full corpus on 8 of 9 benchmarks and was better than a random 25% subset on four, although it was worse on PASTIS. Second, how a layer is used matters as much as whether it is included: Landsat-8/9 improved or matched Sentinel-2-only pretraining on every benchmark. Third, DEM and WorldCover helped as decoder targets and hurt as encoder inputs. Fourth, Sentinel-1 helped mainly TreeSatAI and BioMassters when it was also given at test time. Fifth, a free rule-based template matched a small LLM, a large LLM was about one point better, and users can write captions with any LLM from the same fact sheets.
blocks.zh: 与奥尔莫地基的实验提出了三点. 首先,通过嵌入多样性来选择可以缩小预受训练的体积而损失不大:在10个世纪的运行中,一个AlphaEarth校准的25%Core-S2L2A子集不比9个基准中的8个基准中的完整体更差,而且比4个随机的25%子集更好,尽管PASTIS中的情况更差. 第二,如何使用地层与是否包括地层一样重要:Landsat-8/9改进了每个基准的Sentinel-2的预训或与之相匹配。 第三,DEM和WorldCover作为解码目标提供帮助,并作为编码输入而受到伤害。 第四,Sentinel-1在测试时也提供时主要帮助了TreeSatAI和BioMassters. 第五,一个基于规则的免费模板匹配一个小的LLM,一个大的LLM比它好约一分,用户可以从同一个事实表上用任何LLM来写字幕.

blocks.en: These conclusions are limited: all runs use at most 6.4% of the official OlmoEarth schedule with one pretraining run per configuration, and the captions were scored by a single LLM judge, not by training a vision-language model on them. Future work should (i) repeat the curation comparison with longer schedules and several pretraining seeds, (ii) train on the temporal regimes without padding to a fixed length, so that Monthly and Burst can be compared fairly, (iii) train a vision-language model on the generated tasks to test the language layer downstream, and (iv) add new layers, such as Sentinel-2 L2A or higher resolution imagery, as further subfolders and tables, together with a loading throughput benchmark that quantifies the access efficiency of the format.
blocks.zh: 这些结论是有限的:所有运行时间最多为官方奥尔莫地表的6.4%,每个配置有一个预训运行,而字幕是由一名LLM评委评分,而不是通过在它们上培训一个视觉语言模型来评分. 未来工作应 (一)与更长的时间表和多出预训种子重复校正对比, (二)在不固定长度的情况下就时间制度进行训练,以便能够公平比较"月"和"布尔斯", (三)在生成的任务上训练一个视觉语言模型来测试下游语言层, (四)增加新的地层,如Sentinel-2 L2A或更高的分辨率图像,作为进一步的子文件夹和表格,同时加载吞吐量基准可以量化格式的取用效率.

Each row in the Parquet index
carries an internal:gdal_vsi column encoding a GDAL virtual file-system
path that points directly at the corresponding COG, rather than embedding the pixel
blob in the index itself. Any Parquet-capable engine (PyArrow, Polars, DuckDB, Arrow
bindings in R or Julia) can therefore evaluate filters on column statistics and skip
row groups that do not match before a single byte of imagery is touched; only
the gdal_vsi paths of surviving rows are passed to GDAL, which opens the

Every tile in the global grid is assigned a Sentinel-2 MGRS identifier, a native UTM

clusters; the point closest to each fine-cluster centroid becomes its
representative.

blocks.en:
The collection does not store captions. It stores the data needed to write them, and a code library
( majortom-elliot-tasks , MIT licence Image and Signal Processing Group, Universitat de València [2026] ) builds fact sheets, questions, answers and
captions from the tile layers when they are needed. The only text-side data stored are the precomputed per-tile facts in
the top-level facts/ folder (Table 3 ), which let tasks be built without reading pixels. The
wording is chosen by rules and a seed, so it changes at every epoch. The library uses only the public collection.

(majortom-elliot-tasks,麻省理工学院许可证图像和信号处理组,瓦伦西亚大学[2026年]) 制作概况介绍,问题,答案和
需要时从瓷砖层取出字幕。 唯一存储的文本侧数据是:
顶级事实/文件夹(表3),允许不读取像素而构建任务。 这个
措辞由规则和一个种子选择,因此在每个时代都会有变化。 图书馆只使用公共收藏.

blocks.en:
For each tile, the library collects everything measured about it into a fact sheet. From the
sample metadata it takes the place and administrative names; from the Sentinel-2 and Landsat-8/9 images it computes
indicators of vegetation (NDVI), water, built-up surfaces, snow and burn scars, and the Landsat-8/9 brightness
temperature; from DEM and WorldCover it takes relief and land-cover shares. From the context layers it takes the named
OpenStreetMap features and administrative units, the cloud masks (so that cloudy pixels are ignored), the ERA5 weather on
the acquisition date and the Sentinel-1 backscatter. Every fact is tagged with the sensor that supports it, and a fact
whose sensor is not given to the model is removed, so the model is never asked about something it cannot see, such as a
temperature without Landsat-8/9. Positions are given in words on a 3 × 3 3\times 3 grid (north-west, centre, and so on)
instead of coordinates. For Monthly and Burst tiles the sheet also holds facts that no single image shows: the yearly
cycle of vegetation (peak and low month, number of green-up cycles), changes in water and snow extent, abrupt change
between two dates (for example a burn), which images are too cloudy to use, and the weather over the period.

Each answer is scored from 0 to 1 by a rule that depends on its shape, and an answer that cannot be

fraction 10 percentage points, solar elevation 2°). • Points: a hit inside the reference object’s box, or within 100 grid units of the reference point; boxes:
intersection over union; several points: F1 after a one-to-one match within 100 grid units. • Grids: share of correct cells. Records: key by key. Free text: token F1 against the reference. • Derived answers: the evidence and the answer are scored separately, and the reported score is the answer’s.

blocks.en:
The caption family is written by a rule-based template (version 2) that reads only
the fact sheet. It is a program with fixed rules that fills ready-made sentences with the measured facts and uses no
language model. The caption has one paragraph per sensor group (location and layout, optical, thermal, radar, terrain,
and cloud and weather), and a paragraph is dropped when its sensor is not given to the model. Numbers are turned into
named fractions (28% becomes “a little under three-tenths”, and a zero share is written as “none”); only the
sheet’s own terms are used (Landsat-8/9 gives a brightness temperature, not a surface temperature, and relief under
40 m is not described); up to six named OpenStreetMap features are chosen across kinds (transport, water, settlements,
green areas, landmarks) and placed in compass words. Every statement has several paraphrases, sentences are reordered
if the order does not matter, and a seed picks the wording, so the same tile and seed always give the same text and
other seeds give other wordings of the same facts. A checker re-reads every proportion in a caption against the fact
sheet and reports any that the facts do not support. Users can instead pass their own captions, for example written by
a language model from the same fact sheet. Section 3.4 compares the two options, and
Appendix G shows template examples.

All numbers in Section 3.1 are computed from the TACO metadata tables of the release over all rows, without reading pixels, except when a sample is stated. Images and tiles are row counts of the per-image and per-tile tables. Years are the year of s2:date . Cloudiness is one minus the CloudScore+ clear score
( s2:score ); the cloud fraction of the masks is one minus the clear fraction (thick cloud, thin cloud and shadow) of an image ( ml:cloud_fraction ).
A Sentinel-1 image is valid if at least 90% of its pixels are non-zero ( s1:valid_fraction ≥ 0.9 \geq 0.9 ); a sample has no Sentinel-1 if that fraction is 0 for every image.

Latitude bands use the centroid of each tile ( ml:geometry ). Land-cover shares sum the WorldCover pixel counts of all tiles and divide by the total. blocks.en:
After pretraining the encoder is frozen and the patch tokens are mean-pooled; the evaluation patch size is 4. Classification benchmarks use a k k -nearest-neighbour classifier with k = 20 k=20 .
Segmentation and regression use a linear probe trained for 50 epochs with AdamW at the learning rate and batch size of Table 15 (batch size 128 for MADOS, 8 for PASTIS, Open-Canopy and BioMassters),
with cross-entropy loss (segmentation) or masked mean-squared error (regression). The test metric is that of the probe after epoch 50: validation is computed only once, at the end of training, so no epoch is selected.
Across probe seeds the nearest-neighbour benchmarks differ by at most 0.01 points (So2Sat 0.1) and the linear probes by at most 0.43 points (MADOS).
Inputs are standardized per band with the benchmark’s own training-split mean and standard deviation ( norm_stats_from_pretrained=False , norm_method=standardize );
for TreeSatAI, Open-Canopy and BioMassters these are estimated once from a fixed sample of 96 training tiles (3 frames per tile for multi-frame benchmarks, no-data excluded) and cached.
We report mIoU rather than the framework’s primary metric for MADOS (micro-F1, equal to overall accuracy) and micro-F1 rather than macro-F1 for BigEarthNet.
EuroSAT, BigEarthNet, BrickKiln and MADOS are read from the OlmoEarth research-benchmark copies of GeoBench and MADOS, and So2Sat from the GeoBench copy; TreeSatAI, BioMassters and Open-Canopy are read from their TACO containers.
